rawText:
Your Brain Rot Score is a polite lie. 29/100? That’s the rating of a used car with a cracked windshield. You’ve liked 11 videos total, which is 11 fewer than the number of times you’ve allegedly “done the work” on your “Notion setup for your entire life.”  

RedFlags:  
- 212 videos in “Watch Later” — your digital hoarder instincts are stronger than your willpower.  
- 0 likes in 7 days. Your “self-improvement” obsession is a spectator sport.  
- “Minimalism” + “techHaul” = a cognitive dissonance so loud it deserves its own podcast.  
- 15-minute avg video length. You’re not watching content — you’re auditing it.  
- “I quit dopamine for 30 days” is your most active contribution to self-care.  
- 27.273 lurker index. You’re a ghost in the machine, but the machine’s got your credit card.  

ChannelRoasts:  
- Daily Discipline: You’ve liked one video. Your discipline is a passive-aggressive text reminder.  
- Deep Work Daily: You’ve never deep-worked. Your “focus” is a 4-hour straight lie.  
- Monk Mode Mike: You’ve liked one video. Your monk mode is a 26-minute Notion tutorial.  
- Porch Philosophy: You’ve liked one video. Your philosophy is a 5am routine you’ve never risen for.  
- Wellness Wire: You’ve liked one video. Your wellness is a “digital detox” you’ve never enacted.  

Personality: A walking paradox of hyper-ambition and zero action. You’re the human equivalent of a “Save for Later” folder — all potential, no payoff. Your brain is a museum of “I should’ve” and “I’ll do it tomorrow.”  

ExistentialQuestion: If you’re this inactive while binge-liking self-help, what’s the point of existing?  

ShareCardLine: “You’ve liked 11 videos. None of them are yours.”
